newsitem.title: USA: Maverick Records announces management shift.
newsitem.headline: Maverick Records announces management shift.

text.p: Freddy DeMann said Monday he was relinquishing his title as pop icon Madonna's manager to spend more time overseeing Maverick Records, the successful label the two co-founded five years ago.

"Madonna has always been more than a client. She is a friend, a partner and an extraordinary artist whose destiny has been intertwined with my own for close to 15 years. I am energized by the prospect of continued collaboration and growth with the exciting challenges we face in moving Maverick into the 21st Century," DeMann said.
Caresse Norman, who has functioned as Madonna's co-manager for the past year, will continue in that capacity, managing her career alone.
DeMann and Madonna are co-chief executive officers of Maverick, which has such hit acts as Prodigy, whose "The Fat of The Land" album is currently topping the charts.

Maverick Records, a joint venture with Time Warner Inc.'s Warner Brothers Records Inc. also achieved phenomenal success with Alanis Morissette's "Jagged Little Pill" album, which sold more than 26 million copies and became the biggest selling album by a female artist and one of the biggest selling debut albums of all time.
Under the revised structure, DeMann will shift his responsibilities from management of Madonna's career to a full-time focus on the operation, expansion and long-term strategic planning Maverick.

"The mutual vision that Freddy and I have evolved for the future of Maverick Records now requires his devoting his extraordinary energy and intellect to our record company on a full-time basis," Madonna said.

"It's been an incredible 14-year run. We've made history together and we've broken new ground together. What prevents this from being a sad occasion is the firm conviction that this remarkable friendship and professional alliance will continue to evolve at the same time that we're able to take Maverick Records to an entirely new level."
